items.followUp: Define a point-to-point connection and give one daily-life example.

rubric.why: Checks that the shared nature of a multipoint connection is identified.
rubric.description: States that two or more devices share one communication link.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing a shared link between multiple devices.

rubric.why: Checks that the definition is applied to a suitable real-life example.
rubric.description: Gives a suitable daily-life example, such as several devices connected through one wireless router.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant example.

modelAnswer: A multipoint connection is a communication link shared by two or more devices.
For example, several phones and computers can share one wireless router to access the Internet.

rubric.why: Checks the role of a web server in hosting website content.
rubric.description: Identifies a web server as a computer or program that stores or hosts websites.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying its hosting role.

rubric.why: Checks how a web server provides website content to users.
rubric.description: States that it sends web pages to clients when they request them.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that it responds to client requests.

modelAnswer: A web server is a computer or program that stores and hosts websites.
It sends the requested web pages to a user's computer when the user accesses the website.

items.followUp: What is a URL, and what is it used for?

rubric.why: Checks the correct expansion of ISP.
rubric.description: Expands ISP as Internet Service Provider.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct full form.

rubric.why: Checks the ISP's main service.
rubric.description: Explains that an ISP provides users with access to the Internet.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating its service.

modelAnswer: ISP stands for Internet Service Provider.
It is an organization that provides users with access to the Internet.

items.followUp: Write an HTML tag that creates a hyperlink to another webpage.

rubric.why: Checks the purpose of a hyperlink.
rubric.description: Explains that a hyperlink connects to or opens another webpage or location.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating what the link does.

rubric.why: Checks how a hyperlink is used in a webpage.
rubric.description: Gives the anchor tag with an href attribute, or explains that the user clicks linked text or an image.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct HTML method or clear description of its use.

modelAnswer: A hyperlink connects a webpage to another webpage, document, or location.
In HTML, it is made with an anchor tag, for example: Open page; the user clicks the linked text to open it.

items.followUp: What is an ordered list in HTML, and which tags are used to create it?

rubric.why: Checks that the student understands the meaning of an unordered list.
rubric.description: States that an unordered list presents items without a particular sequence, usually as bullets.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing its order or bullet style.

rubric.why: Checks knowledge of the HTML tags used to create the list.
rubric.description: Names the <ul> tag and the <li> tag.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark when both tags are given.

modelAnswer: An unordered list displays items without a particular order, usually with bullets.
In HTML, the <ul> tag defines the list and each item is written inside an <li> tag.

items.followUp: Describe how you identify the inputs and outputs when designing an algorithm.

rubric.why: Checks that algorithm formulation begins by understanding the problem.
rubric.description: States that the problem and its requirements must be understood or analysed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying problem analysis as a first step.

rubric.why: Checks that required input data is identified.
rubric.description: States that the data required to solve the problem must be determined.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the inputs.

rubric.why: Checks that the expected result is identified.
rubric.description: States that the expected output or result must be determined.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the outputs.

rubric.why: Checks that the solution is expressed and checked as an algorithm.
rubric.description: States that logical steps are arranged and the algorithm is tested or verified.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the stepwise solution and its checking.

modelAnswer: First, understand and analyse the problem and its requirements.
Identify the input data needed to solve the problem.
Determine the output or result that is required.
Arrange the solution as logical steps, then test the algorithm to check that it works correctly.

items.followUp: Name and briefly explain the sender and receiver in a communication system.

rubric.why: Checks identification of the two communicating parties.
rubric.description: Identifies the sender and receiver, and indicates that the sender transmits while the receiver gets the communication.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying and briefly describing both.

rubric.why: Checks understanding of what is communicated.
rubric.description: Explains that the message is the information or data being sent.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the message.

rubric.why: Checks identification of the path used to carry the message.
rubric.description: Explains that the medium or channel carries the message from sender to receiver.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the medium.

rubric.why: Checks understanding of the rules that govern communication.
rubric.description: Explains that protocols are the rules followed for communication between devices.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the protocol.

modelAnswer: Sender and receiver: the sender sends information, and the receiver gets it.
Message: the information or data that is communicated.
Medium or channel: the path through which the message travels from sender to receiver.
Protocol: the rules followed by the devices to communicate.

items.followUp: Define invalid test data and give one example.

rubric.why: Checks that valid test data is distinguished by meeting specified conditions.
rubric.description: States that valid test data satisfies the program's requirements, such as its allowed type, format, or range.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking validity to the specified requirements.

rubric.why: Checks that the definition indicates data acceptable for the program.
rubric.description: Clarifies that the data is suitable for the program to process, for example by being in the permitted range or correct format.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a clear statement of acceptability or a relevant condition.

modelAnswer: Valid test data is input data that satisfies the requirements specified for a program.
It is acceptable for the program to process, for example because it has the correct type or falls within the permitted range.
